items.title: One integrated data model, not two brands, is the strategic asset of the combined platform
items.summary: On 7 May 2026 Vortex Capital Partners acquired 1TIS and a majority stake in TravelSpirit to build one travel ERP platform: together the two systems serve 3,000+ daily users, process roughly €1.5 billion in annual travel revenue and employ about 40 people. Both brands stay live for now, with a single brand and strategy planned later.
items.implication: Every roadmap decision should be judged by whether it deepens the shared product-booking-passenger-payment-supplier record that portals, automation, AI and BI compound on; brand unification is secondary to data-model unification.

items.title: Group-travel depth and tailor-made flexibility are complementary segments to cross-sell, not competing products
items.summary: Livingstone and Vortex describe 1TIS as ERP for the travel industry with a focus on group travel and TravelSpirit as the complementary provider for tailor-made travel operators and DMCs; the investment thesis explicitly combines the two market positions and TravelSpirit adds advisory services for process optimisation across the customer journey.
items.implication: Model group-operations modules as an upsell to tailor-made tenants and the Visual Tour Builder as an upsell to group operators; measure cross-sell rather than treating the two customer groups as separate businesses.

items.title: Low-entry modular pricing sets the commercial model: land on a base package, expand per module and per user
items.summary: 1TIS publishes a €129/month base package (CRM, booking registration, invoicing, mail integration, product management, alerts and documents) with optional modules at €10–€25/month and pricing that scales with user licences. TravelSpirit publishes a Start package from €99/month for 1 user, Professional from €279/month for 3 users, Business from €899/month for 10 users, Enterprise from 30 users on request, and €65/month per extra user.
items.implication: Revenue growth per tenant comes from module attach and seat expansion, so instrument attach rates and seat activation as first-class business outcomes and design onboarding so a €99–€129 tenant reaches its first live booking fast.

items.title: Group operations detail is the moat that generic ERP and booking tools do not have
items.summary: The 1TIS group-travel software allocates buses with fixed pre-reserved seats, generates seating lists for drivers and accommodation rosters, gives tour leaders per-trip participant lists with individual details, sends every change one-to-one to the DMC, and adds a Begeleiders (guide) module at €10/month for guide registration and assignment.
items.implication: Keep seat and room allocation, guide assignment and DMC change synchronisation as deep, opinionated capabilities with their own accuracy and rework KPIs; this is where coach and group operators switch from spreadsheets.

items.title: A portal for every third party turns handling time into self-service
items.summary: 1TIS ships seven sites and portals off the same back office: a bookable customer website, a booking-view page where customers approve quotes, view bookings, pay and retrieve travel documents, a customer portal, a reseller portal for bookings and documents, a supplier portal to approve or decline requests and access room lists, a group-leader portal and a tour-guide portal with participant lists and room assignments.
items.implication: Treat portals as the primary lever on operator handling minutes per booking; measure portal activation and the share of document, payment-status and supplier-confirmation interactions that never reach the desk.

items.title: Visual online proposals decide tailor-made conversion
items.summary: TravelSpirit's Visual Tour Builder is a drag-and-drop itinerary builder with online quote generation and passenger management; Capterra positions the product at medium and large tour operators and agencies in the Netherlands and Belgium selling package deals and customised journeys, with itinerary creation and multi-currency and multi-language support. 1TIS's tailor-made offer stresses that every quote is unique, assembled from standard text blocks, priced per traveller and approved by the client in a 'Mijn omgeving' portal.
items.implication: Optimise proposal build time, version count and online engagement as the conversion funnel for tailor-made specialists, and connect the accepted proposal directly to the trip file and deposit payment.

items.title: Payments, accounting, apps and reviews come from a partner ecosystem, not from the ERP vendor
items.summary: TravelSpirit lists Mollie (payments and payment links), Exact (accounting), Spotler (email marketing), Travel Intelligence (BI), WeCloudIT (telephony), Airtrotter (availability), Travelia and Appit (mobile apps) and Hubby eSIM as partners. The partners are large horizontal platforms: Mollie states more than 250,000 businesses across Europe and a 1,000-strong team, Exact states more than 675,000 companies and 2,000 specialists, and Trustpilot reports 400 million+ reviews with 200,000+ written daily.
items.implication: Invest in an integration hub with connector-health and activation KPIs rather than building payments, ledgers or review engines; partner attach (accounting, payment links, apps, eSIM) is both a retention and an ancillary-revenue lever.

items.title: Flight settlement is a reconciliation job that needs standardised imports, not manual matching
items.summary: IATA's Billing and Settlement Plan is the standard framework for sales reporting, remittance and settlement between 400+ airlines and 59,000+ accredited agents, settling more than $242 billion annually at a 99.99% on-time rate and in operation for over 50 years. TravelSpirit's Flights module imports flight data from GDS and Airtrade and processes settlement statements from IATA HOT and Airtrade.
items.implication: Model flight-ticket records and settlement-file matching as a distinct finance capability with a match-rate KPI; every unmatched ticket is a manual reconciliation at month-end.

items.title: Guarantee-fund participation is a hard, per-booking compliance attach in the Dutch trade
items.summary: SGR has 650 participants and, together with the GGTO fund for smaller operators integrated into SGR since January 2025 (nearly 350 participants), approaches 1,000; the fund reports €220 million own capital and a 200% Solvency II ratio. SGR's consumer-contribution regulation obliges participants to pay a €5 per-person contribution (per booking in some cases) on package travel, linked travel arrangements, transport and accommodation agreements, with the participant that receives the customer's payment liable for the levy.
items.implication: Guarantee-fund levies, participant reporting and the SGR logo on booking confirmations must be native to the booking and invoicing flow; measure report preparation time and on-time filings as finance outcomes.

items.title: The revised Package Travel Directive changes deposit, refund and complaint flows for every organiser
items.summary: Directive (EU) 2015/2302 already obliges organisers to provide insolvency protection, to give clear pre-contractual information, to allow free cancellation when the price rises by more than 8%, and to be liable for performance regardless of who delivers the services. The Commission proposed a revision on 29 November 2023 and Council and Parliament reached a provisional agreement on 2 December 2025: complaints must be acknowledged within 7 days and answered within 60 days, vouchers are allowed as refund alternatives only with traveller consent and are insolvency-protected, the proposed EU-wide 25% downpayment cap was replaced by national limits, and member states get 28 months to transpose.
items.implication: Build deposit schedules, refund and voucher handling, complaint SLAs and pre-contractual information forms as configurable compliance rules per country, ready before transposition deadlines rather than as tenant-by-tenant customisation.

items.title: Dutch holiday demand is large, outbound and car-heavy, which keeps coach and group products alive
items.summary: CBS counts 21.9 million summer holidays in 2025 taken by 10.8 million people, 72% of residents aged 15+; 12.9 million were abroad and 9.0 million domestic, with France (2.15 million), Germany (1.73 million), Spain (1.35 million), Belgium (1.15 million) and Italy (1.11 million) the top foreign destinations. 13.4 million holidays were by car, 4.9 million by plane and 1.7 million by train; participation ranged from 41% in the lowest-income households to 87% in the highest.
items.implication: Departure yielding and capacity decisions for coach and group products should be modelled around nearby European destinations and seasonal peaks; the addressable market for the operators on the platform is measured in millions of trips, not niche volumes.

items.title: European travel is overwhelmingly intra-EU, so multi-country operation is the expansion path
items.summary: Eurostat reports 1.19 billion trips by EU residents in 2024 (up 4.4% on 2023), of which 850 million were domestic (71%) and 250 million to other EU countries (21%), so 92% of trips were intra-EU; residents spent €618 billion, on average €518 per person per trip, with foreign trips averaging 8 nights. Compliance under the Package Travel Directive in one member state is sufficient to sell to consumers in another.
items.implication: Multi-language, multi-currency and per-country compliance rules are the prerequisites for the year-5 horizon beyond the Netherlands and Belgium; DMCs and suppliers across the EU are the natural first cross-border users of the portals.

items.title: The addressable trade is a long tail of small, organised operators that buy through associations and references
items.summary: ANVR has around 400 members, a few large enterprises and a large majority of SMEs; VvKR unites 546 small-scale travel specialists (founded 2011) that all offer a travel guarantee on package tours and carry mandatory liability insurance. TravelSpirit is a member of ANVR and VVKR and states that 100+ travel companies use its software; 1TIS states more than 140 travel organisations across the Netherlands, Belgium and Germany.
items.implication: Go-to-market runs through associations, reference customers and low-friction start packages; measure reference-sourced leads and tenant counts per segment rather than enterprise pipeline alone.

items.title: A 40-person company can only reach ERP-standard status by embedding AI and automation into the office work
items.summary: Vortex's thesis is to build a market-leading travel ERP by enhancing product capabilities, embedding AI, professionalising the organisation and making selective acquisitions; the combined company has about 40 employees and 1TIS states 20 employees who develop everything in-house with Dutch programmers for more than 140 travel organisations. Michiel Stoffels (CEO) and Rico van Loenen (CPO) lead the combination.
items.implication: AI assistants for reply drafting, inbox triage and itinerary drafting are the scaling lever for both the vendor and its tenants; measure assistant acceptance and attach as leading indicators of revenue per FTE on both sides.
